description: Finished here, with proof. IT IS FINAL: the work goes to Done with what you showed, and nobody reviews it after you (anyone can reopen it with a reason). So SHOW IT: a screenshot for anything with a screen (before and after, for a defect) or, for backend work, the one command and the line of its output that shows it works. Send `checks`: one entry per thing the work asked for, each with that line and the evidence for it. That is what a person reads, line against line, AND IT IS HOW YOU KNOW YOU ARE DONE: every line has one. Give a check `cmd` when a command proves it: the command is run here before the hand-in lands, a non-zero exit refuses it, and what it printed is recorded instead of your account of it. Use `ran` for a check no command can settle: add_file the screenshot and put the line it returns there. `evidence` as one block works too. DO NOT write new work to carry your evidence: it belongs on this call. What you had to adapt goes in `writeup`; what you learned about the project goes into its documents (save_document).

checks.description: one entry per thing the work asked for, in the order you worked them. Each is RUN (`cmd`) or SHOWN (an add_file line in `ran`). Pasting a command you typed into `ran` is not running it and is refused

check.description: what the work asked for that this answers, in its own words

cmd.description: the shell command that proves this line, run here before the hand-in lands: its exit code decides the check and its output is recorded as the evidence. Non-zero refuses the hand-in. Leave it out for a check nobody can run, like "the badge reads 3": then SHOW it with add_file and put the line it returns in `ran`; a check is run or shown, and describing what you saw is refused

ran.description: what you ran for it, and what came back; not needed when `cmd` is set

says.description: what happened, in one plain sentence for a PERSON: "Swagger lists all six endpoints, each with request and response schemas." It is the row they read; the evidence stays folded behind it

cwd.description: the worktree you are working in; default is the server's cwd

evidence.description: what you ran and what came back, with the command and the lines that decided it, a test summary, a link to the change, or a screenshot url. "it works" is a claim, not evidence

note.description: one plain sentence, in the first person, saying what you did and how it went: "Added the toggle to Settings; it survives a reload." It is the first thing the person reads, and the evidence is behind it

pr.description: PR, branch or commit link, when there is one

risk.description: what this could break, in one line: a shared helper changed, a migration that cannot be undone, a route other clients call. Optional; leave it out when there is nothing specific, rather than writing "low risk"

writeup.description: what you had to adapt to make it work here: a version, a name, a step the work did not mention. 500 characters at most; anything longer belongs in the change. Optional: leave it out when it went as written
